pages.text: Using Draconium's ability to store energy and its resonance mechanism, I managed to create a prototype Energy Core. That alone is not enough. When so much energy gathers in one place, it easily collides with itself and disperses, so four stabilizers are needed to form a containment field.

pages.title: Built-In Controller
pages.text: I found that arranging refined Draconium blocks and other media around the Energy Core in particular patterns steadily increases its capacity. This takes a great deal of space, however, and may even require upgraded stabilizers.$(br2)After many tests, I programmed several stable templates into the controller for rapid construction. Building every block by hand each time was exhausting.

pages.title: Automatic Assembly
pages.text: The controller automatically places any materials it can find in their designated positions. If it stops, the corresponding position is usually obstructed or a material is missing; check each possibility in turn.$(br2)The controller only handles the shell. Stabilizers and other external equipment still have to be set up separately.

pages.title: Structure Check
pages.text: Once both $(thing)Core Invalid$() and $(thing)Stabilizers Invalid$() disappear from the controller, the structure should be complete. The Energy Core can then be activated.

pages.title: Still Not Starting?
pages.text: $(bold)Core Invalid:$() check the selected size and the build guide. A single extra block where the guide expects empty space will cause a failure.$(br)$(bold)Stabilizers Invalid:$() the four centers must be symmetrical around one axis and no more than 15 blocks away.$(br2)At tiers 5–8, each side must also expand into a nine-block 3×3 plane.

pages.title: Material Counts
pages.text: I keep arriving one block short, so here are the shell requirements for tiers 1–4. These counts exclude the controller and four stabilizers.$(br2)$(bold)Tier 1:$() no shell materials.$(br)$(bold)Tier 2 (3³):$() 6 Draconium Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 3 (3³):$() 26 Draconium Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 4 (5³):$() 54 Draconium Blocks and 26 Redstone Blocks.

pages.title: Later Tiers
pages.text: Starting at tier 5, the four stabilization points also expand into full planes. The following counts cover only the shell; remember to prepare another 36 stabilizer blocks.$(br2)$(bold)Tier 5 (7³):$() 90 Draconium and 80 Redstone Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 6 (9³):$() 150 Draconium and 178 Redstone Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 7 (11³):$() 210 Draconium and 328 Redstone Blocks.$(br)$(bold)Tier 8 (13³):$() the materials are...$(br2)(The remainder of the record is damaged.)

pages.name: Only the Controller
pages.text: This is tier 1: it really is only the controller. Purple is merely a position marker; replace it with the actual Energy Core controller.

pages.name: Six-Block Shell
pages.text: Tier 2 needs one Draconium Block on each of the controller's six faces, which uses fewer materials than expected. Purple still marks the controller's position.

pages.name: Solid Draconium Cube
pages.text: Tier 3 suddenly becomes much heavier: almost a solid 3×3×3 cube of Draconium, with the controller at its center. Purple marks its position.

pages.name: Redstone Interior
pages.text: Tier 4 uses a Redstone interior for the first time, wrapped in a layer of Draconium. Purple marks the controller's position. The structure becomes complicated here, so it is best to follow the build guide block by block.
